The math of absorption, or how to realize that a given thing isn’t for YOU.

“A lot of grown, intelligent people who could sit around for six hours talking about the nuts and bolts of solar panels can’t talk about their jealousy, or God, or death, or their childhood, or money, or sex, or psychedelics, or how to let somebody go when they want to go.
community-s12c.u1c1-emuB:
The Math of Absorption (or How to Not Write for The New Yorker)

Before discussing the article, it will be worthwhile to discuss those who do not wish to discuss the article, who, when faced with the prospect of openly sharing thoughts on their deepest struggles with jealousy, on God and death, on the nature of childhood and money, on sex and psychedelics, and, most of all, what they think about when their lover wants to leave them, would choose to talk for six hours about installing solar panels. This is not to say that these people are not completely intelligent and well-developed adults; indeed, that may well be…
